Definition: from G4253 and G3004; to say beforehand, i.e. predict, forewarn:--foretell, tell before.
BiblicalUsage: Prolego means to say beforehand, to foretell, to forewarn, and its verses carry the whole doctrine of prophecy. Paul told the Thessalonians before that they would suffer tribulation, and the writer to the Hebrews says God limited a certain day, saying in David before. Isaiah said before that a remnant would be left, and Paul said before to the Galatians that any other gospel is accursed.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe saying before is God's signature on his word: what he says beforehand, he brings to pass. That is why I trust the promises still unfulfilled, because the ones already fulfilled prove the pattern.
